strengths: Identifies an important and previously under-explored vulnerability in locate-then-edit model editing paradigms with rigorous theoretical analysis (Theorems G.13, G.16, G.21 and H.3, H.4)
Provides both attack (KSTER) and defense (subspace camouflage) with comprehensive theoretical grounding using elegant mathematical framework (Woodbury matrix identity, spectral analysis)

Comprehensive experimental validation across three LLMs (GPT-J, Llama3-8B, Qwen2.5) and two datasets with extensive ablations demonstrating robustness to candidate pool size, covariance estimation quality, and sequential editing

Strong empirical results with high success rates (~99% subject recall, 88% semantic similarity on CounterFact) and thoughtful analysis of failure modes (bimodal distribution revealing semantic ambiguity and optimization conflicts)
Clear presentation with effective organization, good use of appendices, and honest discussion of limitations and ethical implications in impact statement
Defense mechanism that maintains model utility while providing protection (Table 4: subject rank increases from 50 to 394 with minimal performance degradation at α=5)
weaknesses: Attack requires strong assumptions: candidate pools of subjects and prompts (though robustness shown), white-box access to parameter differences, and access to or ability to estimate covariance matrix C

Significant theory-practice gaps: Assumption G.5/G.6 on δθ-separability violated in practice (Figure 2b shows cosine similarities >0.95 between edited and non-edited subjects); bimodal failure distribution (Figure 3) represents fundamental limitations
Prompt recovery has inherent limitations with only ~50% Top-1 recall on CounterFact, and significant degradation on QA-style datasets (Top-1 recall 0.08-0.40 on zsRE in Table 2)

Defense introduces new failure modes: hallucinations increase substantially with protection level (Table 17: True Fact Recall drops from 0.51 to 0.23 at α=7) and scalability under sequential editing remains unvalidated

Limited experimental scope: relatively small batch sizes (N≤100), no comparison to alternative defense mechanisms (differential privacy, randomization), and gray-box baseline using Jensen-Shannon divergence is weak

Missing analysis on design choices: entropy reduction formulation (Eq. 7) not well justified, decoy subject quality effects unexplored, and practical guidance for selecting α given utility-protection trade-offs unavailable
